criteria.criterion: A test loads the repository's real athena.toml (with its [parallel] section) through Config and passes. A config without [parallel] yields max_concurrency 1. A config with an unknown top-level section is rejected. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: config.rs: REPO_CONFIG = include_str!("../../../athena.toml"). `the_real_athena_toml_parses_with_its_parallel_section` asserts the file contains [parallel] and parses through Config. `without_a_parallel_section_the_drain_is_serial` asserts the value is 1 both when the section is removed and when it is empty. `unknown_keys_are_rejected` rejects an unknown [surprise] section and an unknown key inside [parallel]. `max_concurrency_must_lie_between_one_and_the_ceiling` rejects 0 and 9. All of these passed in both runs.

criteria.criterion: A drain test with bound 1 shows items run strictly in the existing order, and all existing drain tests pass unchanged. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
criteria.evidence: `with_a_bound_of_one_items_run_strictly_in_plan_order_and_alone` asserts the exact log c,a,b (start/end/land) and a peak of 1. `git diff HEAD~1 --numstat` on tests/drain.rs shows 308 lines added and 0 removed, so the existing tests are unchanged. The drain test binary ran 66 tests, all passing. Plan.order is built as the groups flattened (plan.rs:187-191), so working batch by batch keeps the existing order.

criteria.criterion: A drain test with bound 2 and two independent items in one group has both in flight at once (barrier; fails if serial). An item that depends on another starts only after it finishes. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
criteria.evidence: `with_a_bound_of_two_two_independent_items_are_in_flight_at_once` uses a spin barrier: each run waits until 2 are active, giving up after 5 s. The test then asserts peak == 2. A serial drain would reach a peak of only 1, so the assertion would fail. `an_item_that_depends_on_another_starts_only_after_it_has_finished` asserts that 'end a' comes before 'start c' with a bound of 3. All 7 parallel tests passed.

criteria.criterion: Tests show one item's failure or refusal does not stop its siblings, the worker bound is never exceeded, and Stop starts no further item. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: `one_items_failure_or_refusal_does_not_stop_its_siblings`: a fails twice, b lands beside it (peak 2), and v is refused. `the_worker_bound_is_never_exceeded`: 6 independent items with bound 2 give a peak of exactly 2. `a_stop_starts_no_further_item_and_finishes_those_in_flight`: only 2 items start, a and b both land, and c and d stay queued with stop = Requested. All passed.

summary: The change does what the retry asked. `athena drain` now runs the independent items of one plan group concurrently, up to a new `[parallel] max_concurrency`. The default of 1 sends execution through the unchanged serial path. The athena.toml section and the Config field land together, and a test parses the real athena.toml through include_str. I ran cargo test (all targets pass), cargo test -p athena-cli including the 7 new parallel drain tests, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check, all clean. The new tests show concurrency with a barrier that would fail in a serial drain. They also show that a dependent item waits for what it needs, that one item's failure or refusal does not stop its siblings, that the worker bound is never exceeded, that a stop starts no further item, and that jobs running side by side cannot overspend the budget. Existing drain tests are unchanged. The docs and CHANGELOG describe what was built, what remains, and the Send+Sync trait changes. The only finding is minor: a test fix in crates/athena-gate/src/content.rs is not on the deliverables list, though it is necessary and disclosed. All results come from this snapshot.
